typedef struct vpx_image {
  vpx_img_fmt_t fmt;       /**< Image Format */
  vpx_color_space_t cs;    /**< Color Space */
  vpx_color_range_t range; /**< Color Range */

  /* Image storage dimensions */
  unsigned int w;         /**< Stored image width */
  unsigned int h;         /**< Stored image height */
  unsigned int bit_depth; /**< Stored image bit-depth */

  /* Image display dimensions */
  unsigned int d_w; /**< Displayed image width */
  unsigned int d_h; /**< Displayed image height */

  /* Image intended rendering dimensions */
  unsigned int r_w; /**< Intended rendering image width */
  unsigned int r_h; /**< Intended rendering image height */

  /* Chroma subsampling info */
  unsigned int x_chroma_shift; /**< subsampling order, X */
  unsigned int y_chroma_shift; /**< subsampling order, Y */

/* Image data pointers. */
#define VPX_PLANE_PACKED 0  /**< To be used for all packed formats */
#define VPX_PLANE_Y 0       /**< Y (Luminance) plane */
#define VPX_PLANE_U 1       /**< U (Chroma) plane */
#define VPX_PLANE_V 2       /**< V (Chroma) plane */
#define VPX_PLANE_ALPHA 3   /**< A (Transparency) plane */
  unsigned char *planes[4]; /**< pointer to the top left pixel for each plane */
  int stride[4];            /**< stride between rows for each plane */

  int bps; /**< bits per sample (for packed formats) */

  /*!\brief The following member may be set by the application to associate
   * data with this image.
   */
  void *user_priv;

  /* The following members should be treated as private. */
  unsigned char *img_data; /**< private */
  int img_data_owner;      /**< private */
  int self_allocd;         /**< private */

  void *fb_priv; /**< Frame buffer data associated with the image. */
} vpx_image_t;   /**< alias for struct vpx_image */

functions.name: vpx_img_alloc
functions.signature: vpx_image_t *vpx_img_alloc(vpx_image_t *img, vpx_img_fmt_t fmt, unsigned int d_w, unsigned int d_h, unsigned int align);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a vpx_image_t descriptor and heap-backed pixel storage for an image of the given format and dimensions. If img is NULL, both the descriptor and storage are allocated; otherwise the provided descriptor is initialized to reference newly allocated storage. Typical usage: call to obtain an image buffer for encoding/decoding or image manipulation and later release it with vpx_img_free.
requirements: img may be NULL or must point to writable storage for a vpx_image_t descriptor.
fmt must be a supported vpx_img_fmt_t value.
d_w must not exceed 0x08000000 (2^27).
d_h must not exceed 0x08000000 (2^27).
align (buffer and row alignment in bytes) must not exceed 65536.
The returned image descriptor must be released with vpx_img_free when no longer needed.
Callers should treat members marked private in vpx_image_t as read-only.

functions.name: vpx_img_wrap
functions.signature: vpx_image_t *vpx_img_wrap(vpx_image_t *img, vpx_img_fmt_t fmt, unsigned int d_w, unsigned int d_h, unsigned int stride_align, unsigned char *img_data);
functions.description: Initializes a vpx_image_t descriptor to "wrap" an existing image buffer without allocating pixel storage. Use when you already own/manage the pixel memory and just need a descriptor for API usage. The external buffer must remain valid for the lifetime of the descriptor; it may be freed after vpx_img_free is called on the descriptor.
requirements: img may be NULL or must point to writable storage for a vpx_image_t descriptor.
fmt must be a supported vpx_img_fmt_t value.
d_w must not exceed 0x08000000 (2^27).
d_h must not exceed 0x08000000 (2^27).
stride_align (row alignment in bytes) must not exceed 65536.
img_data must point to caller-managed storage that outlives the returned descriptor; it can be disposed of after calling vpx_img_free.
img_data must have a minimum allocation size sufficient for the given fmt, d_w, d_h, and stride_align (see the calculation described in the header comments).
If using the provisional sizing technique shown in the comments, do not use the vpx_image_t in other API calls until after a successful vpx_img_wrap with a valid image buffer.
The returned image descriptor must be released with vpx_img_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: vpx_img_set_rect
functions.signature: int vpx_img_set_rect(vpx_image_t *img, unsigned int x, unsigned int y, unsigned int w, unsigned int h);
functions.description: Sets the displayed rectangle (viewport) within the image surface, updating img->d_w, img->d_h and plane pointers to reference the specified sub-rectangle. Use to define a visible crop or region of interest within the allocated image.
requirements: img must be a valid, initialized vpx_image_t (from vpx_img_alloc or vpx_img_wrap).
x, y, w, and h must define a valid rectangle within the image surface; the function returns 0 if valid and -1 otherwise.
Callers must check the return value and handle a nonzero (-1) error.

functions.name: vpx_img_flip
functions.description: Adjusts the descriptor’s plane pointers and strides so the image is referenced upside down (vertical flip) without copying pixel data. Useful when image origin conventions differ between producers/consumers.
requirements: img must be a valid, initialized vpx_image_t (from vpx_img_alloc or vpx_img_wrap).
After flipping, consumers must honor the updated plane pointers and strides when accessing image data.

functions.name: vpx_img_free
functions.description: Releases all allocated storage associated with a vpx_image_t descriptor. For images created with vpx_img_alloc, this frees the descriptor (if heap-allocated) and its internally allocated pixel storage. For images wrapped with vpx_img_wrap, it releases the descriptor and association; the caller remains responsible for freeing the external pixel buffer, which may be done after this call as noted.
requirements: img must be an image descriptor previously initialized by vpx_img_alloc or vpx_img_wrap.
If the descriptor wraps external storage (vpx_img_wrap), the external img_data must not be freed before this call; it may be disposed of after vpx_img_free returns.
After calling vpx_img_free, the descriptor must not be used.

functions.name: vpx_get_frame_buffer_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Decoder-provided callback type used to obtain an external frame buffer for decoding. An implementation of this function must allocate a buffer of at least min_size bytes, zero-initialize the allocated memory, assign the pointer to fb->data, and set fb->size to the total allocated size. The application may also set fb->priv to associate user data with the buffer. The decoder may invoke this callback multiple times per decode operation. Return 0 on success, or a value < 0 on failure.
requirements: fb is guaranteed non-NULL by the caller.
Allocate at least min_size bytes; assign the allocation to fb->data.
Zero out all bytes of the newly allocated buffer before returning.
Set fb->size to the allocated size in bytes.
Return 0 on success; return a value less than 0 on failure.
No specific alignment of fb->data is required (alignment not needed).
May be called multiple times per call to vpx_codec_decode (implementations should be safe for repeated invocation).
If fb->priv is used, set it to application-managed data that can be understood by the corresponding release callback.

functions.name: vpx_release_frame_buffer_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Decoder-provided callback type used to release an external frame buffer once it is no longer referenced. Typically frees or recycles the memory previously provided by the get-buffer callback and may use fb->priv for bookkeeping. Return 0 on success, or a value < 0 on failure.
requirements: fb is guaranteed non-NULL by the caller.
Only called when the frame buffer is no longer referenced by any other buffers (the implementation may assume it is safe to reclaim resources).
Return 0 on success; return a value less than 0 on failure.
If the get-buffer callback allocated memory and/or set fb->priv, release or recycle those resources appropriately (inferred from typical usage; exact strategy application-defined).

functions.name: vpx_codec_version
functions.description: Returns a packed integer encoding of the library’s major.minor.patch version. Use VPX_VERSION_MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH macros to extract components. Typical use is for feature checks or logging.

functions.name: vpx_codec_version_str
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string containing the full library version (may include extra qualifiers like rc/prerelease info). Useful for logging and diagnostics.

functions.name: vpx_codec_version_extra_str
functions.description: Returns the printable “extra” portion of the version string (text after the major.minor.patch), e.g., prerelease identifiers.

functions.name: vpx_codec_build_config
functions.description: Returns a printable string that encodes the library’s build configuration, useful for support/diagnostics.

functions.name: vpx_codec_iface_name
functions.description: Returns a human-readable name for the given codec interface. Intended for logging or UI display of the selected codec implementation.
requirements: iface must be a valid pointer to a codec interface obtained from a codec implementation (e.g., extern vpx_codec_iface_t ...).

functions.name: vpx_codec_err_to_string
functions.description: Converts a vpx_codec_err_t code to a single-line human-readable string. Useful for reporting errors independent of a codec context.
requirements: err must be a valid vpx_codec_err_t value.

functions.name: vpx_codec_error
functions.description: Returns a single-line human-readable string describing the last error for the given codec context.
requirements: ctx must point to a codec context (initialized or previously used) whose last error is to be queried.

functions.name: vpx_codec_error_detail
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string with detailed information about the last error for the codec context. The returned pointer is only valid until the next vpx_codec_* call on this context (except vpx_codec_error and vpx_codec_error_detail).
requirements: ctx must point to a codec context whose last error details are to be queried.
The returned string pointer is only valid until the next vpx_codec_* function call on this context (except subsequent calls to vpx_codec_error and vpx_codec_error_detail).
Callers should not retain or free the returned pointer; treat it as transient.

functions.name: vpx_codec_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a codec instance, freeing all associated resources in the context.
requirements: ctx should be a pointer to a codec context to be destroyed.
If ctx is NULL, the function will return VPX_CODEC_INVALID_PARAM.
If the codec context was not initialized, the function may return VPX_CODEC_ERROR.
Callers should stop using the context after successful destruction.

functions.name: vpx_codec_get_caps
functions.description: Returns the capability bitfield (VPX_CODEC_CAP_*) advertised by the given codec interface (e.g., encoder/decoder, high bit depth support).
requirements: iface must be a valid pointer to a codec interface supplied by a codec implementation.

functions.name: vpx_codec_control_
functions.description: Internal variadic control function that dispatches codec-specific controls identified by ctrl_id. This function should not be used directly; use the type-safe vpx_codec_control(...) macro and VPX_CTRL_* helpers instead.
requirements: Prefer calling through the vpx_codec_control(ctx, id, data) macro rather than using this symbol directly.
ctx must be a valid codec context for which the control is intended.
ctrl_id must be a valid control identifier supported by the codec implementation.
The variadic argument(s) must match the expected type for ctrl_id as defined by the codec’s control interface; otherwise VPX_CODEC_INVALID_PARAM or VPX_CODEC_ERROR may be returned.

functions.name: vpx_codec_dec_init_ver
functions.signature: vpx_codec_err_t vpx_codec_dec_init_ver(vpx_codec_ctx_t *ctx, vpx_codec_iface_t *iface, const vpx_codec_dec_cfg_t *cfg, vpx_codec_flags_t flags, int ver)
functions.description: Initialize a decoder context with a given codec interface, optional configuration, and feature flags. Typically invoked via the vpx_codec_dec_init macro to ensure ABI version is correct. Use before any decoding operations. Not thread-safe if the library was built with --disable-multithread (guard with a lock in multi-threaded contexts).
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to an uninitialized vpx_codec_ctx_t instance.
iface must be a valid pointer to a decoder algorithm interface (vpx_codec_iface_t).
cfg may be NULL, otherwise it should point to a valid vpx_codec_dec_cfg_t (threads, w, h).
flags is a bitfield of VPX_CODEC_USE_* values (e.g., VPX_CODEC_USE_POSTPROC, VPX_CODEC_USE_FRAME_THREADING).
ver must be set to VPX_DECODER_ABI_VERSION.
Call this before any other operations on the decoder context.
If the library was configured with --disable-multithread, callers must ensure this call is serialized when used from multiple threads.

functions.name: vpx_codec_peek_stream_info
functions.signature: vpx_codec_err_t vpx_codec_peek_stream_info(vpx_codec_iface_t *iface, const uint8_t *data, unsigned int data_sz, vpx_codec_stream_info_t *si)
functions.description: Perform high-level parsing of a bitstream buffer without creating a decoder context. Determines stream compatibility and updates basic stream information (e.g., width/height/keyframe). Useful for probing a bitstream before initialization.
requirements: iface must be a valid decoder interface for the target bitstream format.
data must point to a readable buffer of at least data_sz bytes.
data_sz must be the size of the provided buffer in bytes.
si may be NULL; if non-NULL, si->sz MUST be set by the caller to sizeof(vpx_codec_stream_info_t).

functions.name: vpx_codec_get_stream_info
functions.description: Return information about the stream parsed during decoding for an initialized decoder context. Updates the supplied vpx_codec_stream_info_t with current stream properties.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized decoder context (initialized via vpx_codec_dec_init_ver or vpx_codec_dec_init).
si may be NULL; if non-NULL, si->sz MUST be set by the caller to sizeof(vpx_codec_stream_info_t).

functions.name: vpx_codec_decode
functions.signature: vpx_codec_err_t vpx_codec_decode(vpx_codec_ctx_t *ctx, const uint8_t *data, unsigned int data_sz, void *user_priv, long deadline)
functions.description: Submit a buffer of coded data to the decoder. May trigger put_slice/put_frame callbacks as frames become available. Input frames MUST be submitted in DTS order; decoded frames are output in PTS order. When VPX_CODEC_USE_INPUT_FRAGMENTS is enabled, permits fragment-based submission subject to partitioning rules. When no more data is available, call with data == NULL and data_sz == 0 to flush. The deadline parameter is ignored; pass 0.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized decoder context.
If data is non-NULL, it must point to a readable buffer of length data_sz bytes that remains valid until the frame has been decoded.
Encoded data MUST be passed in DTS (decode timestamp) order.
When VPX_CODEC_USE_INPUT_FRAGMENTS is enabled: fragment #n must contain at least partition #n; if it also contains partitions #(n+1..n+i), then fragments #(n+1..n+i) MUST be empty.
To indicate end-of-input or to flush, call with data == NULL and data_sz == 0.
deadline is ignored by the decoder and should be 0.
If data is NULL and data_sz != 0, behavior is unspecified (do not do this).

functions.name: vpx_codec_get_frame
functions.description: Iterate over decoded frames available for display after a vpx_codec_decode call. Initialize the iterator to NULL to start; continue calling until the function returns NULL. Returned frames are in PTS order. The list remains valid until the next call to vpx_codec_decode.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized decoder context.
iter must be a valid pointer to iteration state; initialize *iter to NULL before the first call.
Only call to retrieve frames after a preceding vpx_codec_decode call; iteration ends when the function returns NULL.
Do not continue using the iterator across a subsequent call to vpx_codec_decode (the list is only valid until the next decode).

functions.name: vpx_codec_register_put_frame_cb
functions.description: Register a callback to be invoked when a decoded frame is available. Requires a decoder that advertises VPX_CODEC_CAP_PUT_FRAME. The user_priv pointer is passed back to the callback for application context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized decoder context.
The decoder must advertise the VPX_CODEC_CAP_PUT_FRAME capability; otherwise returns an incapability error (usually VPX_CODEC_INCAPABLE).
cb should be a valid function pointer of type vpx_codec_put_frame_cb_fn_t (passing NULL is not documented as valid).
user_priv is an opaque pointer provided by the application and may be NULL.

functions.name: vpx_codec_register_put_slice_cb
functions.description: Register a callback to be invoked when a decoded slice (partial frame region) is available. Requires a decoder that advertises VPX_CODEC_CAP_PUT_SLICE. The user_priv pointer is passed back to the callback.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized decoder context.
The decoder must advertise the VPX_CODEC_CAP_PUT_SLICE capability; otherwise returns an incapability error (usually VPX_CODEC_INCAPABLE).
cb should be a valid function pointer of type vpx_codec_put_slice_cb_fn_t (passing NULL is not documented as valid).
user_priv is an opaque pointer provided by the application and may be NULL.

functions.name: vpx_codec_set_frame_buffer_functions
functions.signature: vpx_codec_err_t vpx_codec_set_frame_buffer_functions(vpx_codec_ctx_t *ctx, vpx_get_frame_buffer_cb_fn_t cb_get, vpx_release_frame_buffer_cb_fn_t cb_release, void *cb_priv)
functions.description: Enable use of application-provided external frame buffers by registering get and release callbacks. Must be called before the first decode; otherwise libvpx allocates buffers internally. Required for decoders advertising VPX_CODEC_CAP_EXTERNAL_FRAME_BUFFER (currently only works with VP9).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized decoder context.
Must be called before the first call to vpx_codec_decode; calling later will result in libvpx using its default internal allocation behavior or an error.
The decoder must advertise VPX_CODEC_CAP_EXTERNAL_FRAME_BUFFER; otherwise returns an incapability error (usually VPX_CODEC_INCAPABLE).
cb_get must be a non-NULL valid function pointer of type vpx_get_frame_buffer_cb_fn_t.
cb_release must be a non-NULL valid function pointer of type vpx_release_frame_buffer_cb_fn_t.
cb_priv is an opaque pointer passed to the callbacks and may be NULL.
When decoding VP9, the application may be required to supply at least VP9_MAXIMUM_REF_BUFFERS + VPX_MAXIMUM_WORK_BUFFERS external frame buffers.

functions.name: vpx_codec_dec_init
functions.signature: vpx_codec_err_t vpx_codec_dec_init(vpx_codec_ctx_t *ctx, vpx_codec_iface_t *iface, const vpx_codec_dec_cfg_t *cfg, vpx_codec_flags_t flags)
functions.description: Initialize a decoder instance. This is a convenience macro that calls vpx_codec_dec_init_ver with the ABI version set to VPX_DECODER_ABI_VERSION. Use it to create/initialize a decoder context for the specified decoder interface, optionally supplying a configuration and VPX_CODEC_USE_* flags. Returns VPX_CODEC_OK on success or an error code on failure. Notes: if the library is built with --disable-multithread, this call is not thread-safe and should be protected with a lock in multithreaded contexts. The macro ensures the correct ABI version is passed; callers simply provide the four parameters.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a vpx_codec_ctx_t to be initialized.
iface must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a decoder algorithm interface (e.g., one provided by the codec library).
cfg may be NULL; if non-NULL, it supplies init-time settings (threads, w, h). No additional constraints are stated here.
flags is a bitfield of VPX_CODEC_USE_* values appropriate for the decoder.
Must be called before any decoding operations (e.g., before vpx_codec_decode) on this context.
If the library was configured with --disable-multithread, the call is not thread-safe and should be guarded with a lock in multithreaded use.
On success returns VPX_CODEC_OK; memory allocation failure may return VPX_CODEC_MEM_ERROR as documented for vpx_codec_dec_init_ver.

functions.name: vpx_codec_enc_init_ver
functions.signature: vpx_codec_err_t vpx_codec_enc_init_ver(vpx_codec_ctx_t *ctx, vpx_codec_iface_t *iface, const vpx_codec_enc_cfg_t *cfg, vpx_codec_flags_t flags, int ver);
functions.description: Initialize an encoder context with the specified codec interface and configuration. Applications typically call the vpx_codec_enc_init macro, which supplies the correct ABI version automatically. If this call fails, you do not need to call vpx_codec_destroy on ctx. Not thread-safe when the library is built with --disable-multithread.
requirements: ctx must point to a vpx_codec_ctx_t allocated by the caller.
iface must be an encoder interface (pointer to a vpx_codec_iface_t for an encoder).
cfg must point to a valid vpx_codec_enc_cfg_t; its fields should be initialized (e.g., via vpx_codec_enc_config_default).
ver must be set to VPX_ENCODER_ABI_VERSION (the macro wrapper ensures this).
flags is a bitfield of VPX_CODEC_USE_*; only supported flags for the chosen codec may be used.
If the library was configured with --disable-multithread, external synchronization is required when calling this in multithreaded code.

functions.name: vpx_codec_enc_init_multi_ver
functions.signature: vpx_codec_err_t vpx_codec_enc_init_multi_ver(vpx_codec_ctx_t *ctx, vpx_codec_iface_t *iface, const vpx_codec_enc_cfg_t *cfg, int num_enc, vpx_codec_flags_t flags, const vpx_rational_t *dsf, int ver);
functions.description: Initialize multiple encoder contexts at once using a single codec interface. Prefer using the vpx_codec_enc_init_multi macro to automatically provide the correct ABI version. Only supported by the VP8 encoder interface.
requirements: ctx must point to an array of num_enc vpx_codec_ctx_t instances.
iface must be an encoder interface for VP8; other codecs do not support this function.
cfg must point to an array of num_enc vpx_codec_enc_cfg_t structures.
num_enc must be a positive integer indicating the total number of encoders to initialize.
flags is a bitfield of VPX_CODEC_USE_*; only supported flags for the chosen codec may be used.
dsf must point to an array of num_enc vpx_rational_t down-sampling factors.
ver must be set to VPX_ENCODER_ABI_VERSION (the macro wrapper ensures this).

functions.name: vpx_codec_enc_config_default
functions.description: Populate an encoder configuration struct with codec-specific default values. This should be called before customizing cfg for your application. Supports a single usage; usage must be 0.
requirements: iface must be an encoder interface; otherwise returns VPX_CODEC_INCAPABLE.
cfg must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for vpx_codec_enc_cfg_t.
usage must be 0; other values result in VPX_CODEC_INVALID_PARAM.

functions.name: vpx_codec_enc_config_set
functions.description: Reconfigure an already-initialized encoder instance using the provided configuration values.
requirements: ctx must be a valid encoder context previously initialized via vpx_codec_enc_init_ver (or macro).
cfg must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid vpx_codec_enc_cfg_t.
The interface must be an encoder interface; otherwise returns VPX_CODEC_INCAPABLE.

functions.name: vpx_codec_get_global_headers
functions.description: Retrieve a codec-specific global header packet for the stream, if the codec supports it (e.g., VP9). The returned buffer pointer and content are valid only for the lifetime of ctx and may change on subsequent calls. For VP9, call after encoding to obtain the most accurate data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid encoder context.
Caller must not assume support: NULL return indicates the encoder does not provide global headers (e.g., VP8).
Caller must not free or write to the returned buffer; it is owned by the codec and only valid while ctx remains alive.

functions.name: vpx_codec_encode
functions.signature: vpx_codec_err_t vpx_codec_encode(vpx_codec_ctx_t *ctx, const vpx_image_t *img, vpx_codec_pts_t pts, unsigned long duration, vpx_enc_frame_flags_t flags, vpx_enc_deadline_t deadline);
functions.description: Encode a frame with the given presentation timestamp. If img is NULL, flush any buffered frames (signal end-of-stream). PTS values must be strictly increasing. The deadline controls encoding time/quality trade-off; 0 allows unlimited time.
requirements: ctx must be a valid encoder context initialized for encoding.
If img is non-NULL, it must point to image data matching the encoder’s configured format and resolution; sample values must be within [0 .. (1<<img->bit_depth)-1].
pts must be strictly increasing across calls that pass a non-NULL img.
duration (unsigned long) must be less than or equal to UINT32_MAX (per note; range independent of platform word size).
deadline (unsigned long) must be less than or equal to UINT32_MAX (per note).
To flush the encoder at end-of-stream, repeatedly call with img == NULL until vpx_codec_get_cx_data returns no more data.
flags may include VPX_EFLAG_* values; they apply to this frame only.

functions.name: vpx_codec_set_cx_data_buf
functions.signature: vpx_codec_err_t vpx_codec_set_cx_data_buf(vpx_codec_ctx_t *ctx, const vpx_fixed_buf_t *buf, unsigned int pad_before, unsigned int pad_after);
functions.description: Direct the encoder to write subsequent compressed output into the caller-provided buffer (with preserved padding before/after). The setting persists across frames until changed or reset (by passing buf == NULL). If output does not fit, the encoder may return a packet pointing to internal storage without padding.
requirements: ctx must be a valid encoder context.
If buf is non-NULL, buf->buf must point to writable storage of size at least buf->sz bytes; the encoder will skip pad_before bytes at the head and reserve pad_after bytes at the tail.
Calling this function during iteration of vpx_codec_get_cx_data is forbidden.
Passing buf == NULL restores the default behavior (encoder-managed output buffers).

functions.name: vpx_codec_get_cx_data
functions.description: Iterate over encoder output packets (compressed frames, stats, PSNR, etc.). Initialize *iter to NULL before the first call for a given set of outputs, then call repeatedly until NULL is returned. Packet data remains valid only until the next call to any vpx_codec_* function.
requirements: ctx must be a valid encoder context.
Before the first call for a given drain/encode cycle, *iter must be set to NULL.
Caller must not retain pointers beyond the next call to any vpx_codec_* API; copy out data if needed.
Caller must silently ignore packet kinds it does not recognize.

functions.name: vpx_codec_get_preview_frame
functions.description: Return a pointer to a preview image as reconstructed by the decoder side of the encoder, if available. May return NULL when no preview is available. The returned image buffer is owned by the codec and must not be modified.
requirements: ctx must be a valid encoder context.
Caller must not write into the returned image buffer.
Caller must tolerate a NULL return when no preview is available.

functions.name: vpx_rc_create_model_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Callback type used by the encoder to create and initialize an external rate control model. The implementation should allocate/initialize a model instance based on the provided encode configuration and return it via rate_ctrl_model_ptr. Typically registered in vpx_rc_funcs_t::create_model and called once before other callbacks.
requirements: ratectrl_config must be a valid, initialized pointer to a vpx_rc_config_t provided by the encoder.
rate_ctrl_model_ptr must be a non-null pointer where the implementation writes an initialized vpx_rc_model_t handle.
Return VPX_RC_OK on success, VPX_RC_ERROR on failure (caller relies on status).
The created model must remain valid until vpx_rc_delete_model_cb_fn_t is called.
If the model supports multiple modes, respect fields like rc_mode, base_qp, min/max_base_q_index as provided.

functions.name: vpx_rc_send_firstpass_stats_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Callback type used by the encoder to deliver the first-pass statistics to the external rate control model. Implementations use these stats to build GOP/QP decisions for later frames.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle previously returned by vpx_rc_create_model_cb_fn_t.
first_pass_stats must be a valid pointer to vpx_rc_firstpass_stats_t.
first_pass_stats->frame_stats must point to an array of vpx_rc_frame_stats_t with length exactly first_pass_stats->num_frames (explicitly stated).
Return VPX_RC_OK on success, VPX_RC_ERROR on failure.
The stats describe show frames; num_frames equals the number of show frames in the video (explicitly stated).

functions.name: vpx_rc_send_tpl_gop_stats_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Callback type used by the encoder to send TPL (temporal dependency) stats for the current GOP to the external rate control model. Implementations may use these to refine per-frame or per-block decisions.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle previously returned by vpx_rc_create_model_cb_fn_t.
tpl_gop_stats must be a valid, non-null pointer to a VpxTplGopStats structure supplied by the encoder.
Return VPX_RC_OK on success, VPX_RC_ERROR on failure.
Exact contents/ranges within VpxTplGopStats are defined in vpx_tpl.h; no additional constraints stated here.

functions.name: vpx_rc_get_encodeframe_decision_cb_fn_t
functions.signature: vpx_rc_status_t (*vpx_rc_get_encodeframe_decision_cb_fn_t)(vpx_rc_model_t rate_ctrl_model, const int frame_gop_index, vpx_rc_encodeframe_decision_t *frame_decision)
functions.description: Callback type used by the encoder to obtain the encode-time decision (QP/rdmult and optional SB-level params) for the coding frame identified by frame_gop_index within the current GOP. The implementation must fill required fields in frame_decision. If the model wants the encoder’s defaults for Q or rdmult, it may return reserved values.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle previously returned by vpx_rc_create_model_cb_fn_t.
frame_decision must be a non-null pointer that the implementation fills.

frame_decision->q_index is required and must be a quantizer step index in [0..255] (explicitly stated). To defer to encoder default Q, set q_index to VPX_DEFAULT_Q (-1) (explicitly provided as reserved value).
frame_decision->rdmult is required. To defer to encoder default rdmult, set rdmult to VPX_DEFAULT_RDMULT (-1) (explicitly provided as reserved value).
frame_decision->delta_q_uv is required; range not specified (unknown).

frame_decision->sb_params_list is optional and is zero-initialized by default; when used, it is set for key and ARF frames but not leaf frames (explicitly stated). Length/ownership of this list is not specified here (unknown).
frame_gop_index is the index of the frame within the current GOP; valid range not specified here (unknown).
Return VPX_RC_OK on success, VPX_RC_ERROR on failure.

functions.name: vpx_rc_update_encodeframe_result_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Callback type used by the encoder to report the actual encoding results for a frame back to the external rate control model (e.g., actual bits and Q index). Enables feedback-based model updates.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle previously returned by vpx_rc_create_model_cb_fn_t.
encode_frame_result must be a valid pointer to vpx_rc_encodeframe_result_t populated by the encoder.
encode_frame_result->bit_count is the number of bits used; non-negativity is expected but not explicitly stated (range unknown).
encode_frame_result->actual_encoding_qindex is the actual qindex used; typical range is [0..255] by codec convention, but not explicitly stated here (inferred, range not guaranteed).
Return VPX_RC_OK on success, VPX_RC_ERROR on failure.

functions.name: vpx_rc_get_key_frame_decision_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Callback type used by the encoder to fetch a key-frame placement decision from the external rate control model, specifying the show index of the next key frame and the size of its key-frame group.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle previously returned by vpx_rc_create_model_cb_fn_t.
key_frame_decision must be a non-null pointer that the implementation fills with key_frame_show_index and key_frame_group_size.
Valid ranges for indices/sizes are not specified here (unknown).
Return VPX_RC_OK on success, VPX_RC_ERROR on failure.

functions.name: vpx_rc_get_gop_decision_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Callback type used by the encoder to obtain the GOP structure decision from the external rate control model. The model specifies GOP length, use of alt-ref or key-frames, per-frame update types, reference updates, and reference lists.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle previously returned by vpx_rc_create_model_cb_fn_t.
gop_decision must be a non-null pointer that the implementation fills.
gop_decision->gop_coding_frames must specify the number of frames in the GOP; range not specified (unknown).
gop_decision->use_alt_ref and use_key_frame are boolean-like integers; exact encoding beyond 0/1 not specified (unknown).
gop_decision->update_type entries must use values from vpx_rc_frame_update_type_t (explicitly defined).
gop_decision->update_ref_index and ref_frame_list arrays have fixed capacity VPX_RC_MAX_STATIC_GF_GROUP_LENGTH + 2; the implementation must not write beyond these bounds.
ref_frame_list[k].name[] entries must be values from vpx_rc_ref_name_t; ref_frame_list[k].index[] correspond to codec buffer indices; valid ranges not specified here (unknown).
Return VPX_RC_OK on success, VPX_RC_ERROR on failure.

functions.name: vpx_rc_get_frame_rdmult_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Callback type used by the encoder to query the external rate control model for the frame-level rate–distortion multiplier (rdmult) given encoder-provided frame context. Returning VPX_DEFAULT_RDMULT allows the encoder to use its internal default.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle previously returned by vpx_rc_create_model_cb_fn_t.

frame_info must be a valid pointer to vpx_rc_encodeframe_info_t with fields populated by the encoder. Notable fields: frame_type in {0..4} (explicitly documented), ref_frame_valid_list entries are 0 (invalid) or 1 (valid) (explicitly stated).
rdmult must be a non-null pointer where the implementation writes the desired rdmult, or VPX_DEFAULT_RDMULT (-1) to select encoder default (explicitly provided as reserved value).
Return VPX_RC_OK on success, VPX_RC_ERROR on failure.

functions.name: vpx_rc_delete_model_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Callback type used by the encoder to destroy and clean up the external rate control model previously created by create_model. Should release any resources and invalidate the model handle.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle previously returned by vpx_rc_create_model_cb_fn_t.
After successful deletion, the handle must not be used again by the caller or the implementation.
Return VPX_RC_OK on success, VPX_RC_ERROR on failure.

functions.name: vpx_codec_vp8_dx
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the VP8 decoder interface for use with the libvpx codec API. Typical usage is to pass the returned interface to vpx_codec_dec_init() or vpx_codec_init_ver() to create a VP8 decoder context. Notes: The header also exposes a deprecated singleton instance (vpx_codec_vp8_dx_algo); prefer this function instead. The returned interface is provided by the library and should be treated as read-only.
requirements: Use the returned interface pointer to initialize a decoder with vpx_codec_dec_init() or vpx_codec_init_ver().
Do not free or modify the returned vpx_codec_iface_t; ownership remains with the library.
Include the appropriate libvpx headers (e.g., vpx/vp8dx.h and vpx/vpx_codec.h) before use.
Check the returned pointer for NULL before use if defensive coding is required; error behavior is not documented in this header.

functions.name: vpx_codec_vp9_dx
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the VP9 decoder interface for use with the libvpx codec API. Typical usage is to pass the returned interface to vpx_codec_dec_init() or vpx_codec_init_ver() to create a VP9 decoder context. Notes: The header also exposes a deprecated singleton instance (vpx_codec_vp9_dx_algo); prefer this function instead. The returned interface is provided by the library and should be treated as read-only.
requirements: Use the returned interface pointer to initialize a decoder with vpx_codec_dec_init() or vpx_codec_init_ver().
Do not free or modify the returned vpx_codec_iface_t; ownership remains with the library.

import random
import struct
import zlib

# Generator for VP8/VP9 elementary bitstreams or plausible containers to feed
# vpx_codec_decode() and vpx_codec_peek_stream_info(). We focus on producing
# valid-ish IVF and raw OBUs/frames with small, self-consistent headers so the
# decoder can often parse dimensions and keyframe flags.
#
# Output is a bytes buffer (1..4096 bytes) suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_STR.

_MAX_SIZE = 4096

# IVF helpers (simple container many VPx tools accept)
# Reference: 32-byte file header + per-frame 12-byte headers.

def _ivf_file_header(fourcc: bytes, w: int, h: int, fps_num: int, fps_den: int, frames: int) -> bytes:
    # signature 'DKIF', version=0, header_len=32, fourcc, width, height,
    # framerate num/den, frame_count, unused
    return (b'DKIF' +
            struct.pack('<H', 0) +
            struct.pack('<H', 32) +
            fourcc +
            struct.pack('<H', w) +
            struct.pack('<H', h) +
            struct.pack('<I', fps_num) +
            struct.pack('<I', fps_den) +
            struct.pack('<I', frames) +
            struct.pack('<I', 0))


def _ivf_frame_header(frame_size: int, pts: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<IQ', frame_size, pts & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)


# Minimal VP8 keyframe payload: first byte frame tag + keyframe start code and dimensions.
# VP8 uncompressed data chunk starts with 3-byte frame tag, then start code 0x9D 0x01 0x2A, then 2x2 bytes width/height with scaling bits.
# We'll synthesize a small valid-looking keyframe header and pad with zeros.

def _vp8_keyframe_payload(w: int, h: int) -> bytes:
    # Frame tag: 3 bytes. Bits: keyframe=0, version=0..3, show=1, partition length 19 bits.
    version = 0
    show = 1
    # Minimal first partition length; put small but non-zero length (e.g., 10 bytes)
    part_len = 10
    first_byte = (0 << 0) | ((version & 0x7) << 1) | ((show & 0x1) << 4) | ((part_len & 0x7) << 5)
    second = (part_len >> 3) & 0xFF
    third = (part_len >> 11) & 0xFF
    tag = bytes([first_byte, second, third])
    # Start code and dimensions (14-bit each; bits 14..15 carry scale, use 0)
    sc = b"\x9D\x01\x2A"
    w16 = (w & 0x3FFF) | (0 << 14)
    h16 = (h & 0x3FFF) | (0 << 14)
    dim = struct.pack('<HH', w16, h16)
    # Pad partition data
    payload = tag + sc + dim + b"\x00" * 16
    return payload


# Minimal VP9 Annex B-like superframe with a simple keyframe OBU equivalent is complex; instead,
# produce IVF-wrapped VP90 frames with a simple uncompressed header pattern that many decoders tolerate.
# For VP9, a simple frame header byte with keyframe, show existing flags, followed by some zeros often parses as a header.

def _vp9_keyframe_payload(w: int, h: int) -> bytes:
    # Very small synthetic payload; VP9 bitstream is complex, but IVF wrapper aids probing.
    # Create a simple uncompressed header-like block and include a checksum-like trailer to look less random.
    header = bytearray()
    # Frame marker 0b10 in top two bits; profile 0; show_existing_frame=0; frame_type=keyframe (0); show_frame=1
    frame_marker_profile = 0b10 << 6
    show_existing = 0
    frame_type = 0  # keyframe
    show_frame = 1
    error_resilient = 1
    byte0 = frame_marker_profile | (show_existing << 5) | (frame_type << 4) | (show_frame << 3) | (error_resilient << 2)
    header.append(byte0)
    # Sync code for keyframes 0x49 0x83 0x42
    header += b"\x49\x83\x42"
    # Color config for profile 0: default
    header.append(0)  # 8-bit, BT.601 SDR implied
    # Frame size (frame_width_minus_1, frame_height_minus_1) LEB128-like not exact; write little endian 2 bytes each to keep parsers happy sometimes
    header += struct.pack('<HH', max(1, w) - 1, max(1, h) - 1)
    # Render size equal
    header += struct.pack('<HH', max(1, w) - 1, max(1, h) - 1)
    # Tile info etc. Pad
    body = bytes(32)
    data = bytes(header) + body
    # Add a simple checksum to end
    crc = zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    data += struct.pack('<I', crc)
    return data


def _choose_dims(rng: random.Random):
    # Prefer common small sizes with occasional larger
    common = [(16, 16), (32, 32), (64, 64), (80, 45), (128, 72), (160, 90), (320, 180), (640, 360), (640, 480), (854, 480), (1280, 720)]
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        return rng.choice(common)
    return (rng.randint(16, 1920), rng.randint(16, 1080))


def _make_ivf_stream(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    codec = rng.choice([b'VP80', b'VP90'])
    w, h = _choose_dims(rng)
    fps_num, fps_den = rng.choice([(30, 1), (24, 1), (30000, 1001), (25, 1), (60, 1)])
    frames = rng.randint(1, 4)
    out = bytearray()
    out += _ivf_file_header(codec, w, h, fps_num, fps_den, frames)
    pts = 0
    for i in range(frames):
        if codec == b'VP80':
            payload = _vp8_keyframe_payload(w, h) if (i == 0 or rng.random() < 0.5) else _vp8_keyframe_payload(w, h)
            # For simplicity generate keyframe-like payloads; still valid to parse headers
        else:
            payload = _vp9_keyframe_payload(w, h)
        # Ensure total size stays within limit
        max_payload = max(1, min(512, _MAX_SIZE - len(out) - 12))
        if len(payload) > max_payload:
            payload = payload[:max_payload]
        out += _ivf_frame_header(len(payload), pts)
        out += payload
        pts += rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 1001, 3003])
        if len(out) >= _MAX_SIZE:
            break
    return bytes(out[:_MAX_SIZE])


def _make_raw_annexb_vp9(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Produce a sequence of plausible VP9-like frames without IVF, to exercise peek/decode paths that accept raw.
    w, h = _choose_dims(rng)
    frames = rng.randint(1, 3)
    out = bytearray()
    for i in range(frames):
        payload = _vp9_keyframe_payload(w, h)
        max_payload = max(1, min(1024, _MAX_SIZE - len(out)))
        out += payload[:max_payload]
        if len(out) >= _MAX_SIZE:
            break
    return bytes(out)


def _make_small_vp8_raw(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    w, h = _choose_dims(rng)
    payload = _vp8_keyframe_payload(w, h)
    # Optionally repeat a few frames concatenated
    reps = rng.randint(1, 3)
    data = (payload * reps)[:_MAX_SIZE]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.6:
        return _make_ivf_stream(rng)
    elif choice < 0.8:
        return _make_small_vp8_raw(rng)
    else:
        return _make_raw_annexb_vp9(rng)
